_doc: NPC_AI_SPEC §8 — LOD tier thresholds and rates.
Tier is assigned by AgentManager: a different region is always D; in
frustum and nearer than nearDistance is A; in frustum beyond it is B —
UNLESS the active region is windowed (a destination), in which case B
also requires staying inside that region's current nav-window bound
(iteration 2.7; the bound itself lives in src/ai/config/navgrid.json's
destination.halfExtent, not a second copy here); out of frustum in the
same region, or past that bound, is C. Fixed regions (home, the Sealed
Crypt) have no such bound — B stays unbounded there.
`steering` is declared here for phases 2-3 to read; phase 1 has no
locomotion to apply it to.
thinkBudgetPerFrame is the hard cap on thinks dispatched in one frame
across ALL agents (§8: never think everyone on one frame).
Wave 11 / phase 8 — two additions, both closing gaps the table above only
implied.
farDistance (60) is B's missing FAR bound. §8's own B row reads '15 m to
region's nav-window edge', which silently assumes every region has a
window; the two fixed regions (home ±56 m, the Crypt) don't, so an agent
90 m down the meadow sat on B — full steering, 5 Hz thinks — purely for
being inside a long third-person view frustum. 60 is not a new opinion:
it is exactly GRAPHICS_PROFILES.performance.characterLodDistance
(game/graphicsProfiles.ts), the distance this project already decided a
rigged character stops being worth DRAWING, measured the same way against
the same camera (RiggedFigure.tsx's own cull uses camera distance, and
its comment already points at this file for the ~5 Hz check rate). One
number, two systems, no second copy to drift. Home's ±56 m half-extent
means this only ever binds across the diagonal of the map or in a large
destination diorama, and never for anything close enough to read.
steering.* is what makes `steering` above cost something. Until phase 8
the field was computed per tier and consumed by nothing but the debug
overlay's own text: every agent paid a full navSteer + anchor resolve on
EVERY render frame regardless of tier, so LOD throttled thinking and not
movement, which is the more expensive half for a walking agent.
simplifiedInterval — tier C runs the steering branch this often instead
of every frame, advancing by the whole banked dt so average speed is
unchanged (~6.7 Hz vs 60: a 9x cut). C is out of frustum or 60 m+
away by definition, so the residual is a ~13 cm hop in a shadow.
teleportInterval — tier D's §8 'coarse step'. 2 s deliberately matches
tier D's own 0.5 Hz thinkHz: one jump per think, not a second cadence
to reason about.
teleportMaxStep — a hard metre cap on one jump, so a long banked dt (a
backgrounded tab, a tier flip) can never fling an agent across the
map. 4 m clears the honest worst case (RUN_SPEED 1.6 x 2 s = 3.2 m).
rendererStaleSec — how long after a renderer last drove an agent the
tier-D sweep still treats it as somebody else's job. See
stepUnrenderedAgents() in core/Locomotion.ts for why that guard is a
timestamp and not an invariant.
reentrySnapCells — §8's 'snap it to the nearest valid navmesh point'
when a tier-D agent comes back into view, in NavGrid cells (cellSize
1.0 m today, config/navgrid.json). Matches NavGrid.nearestWalkable's
own default radius, which findPath has used since before this system.
